page: Amazon Web Services m8id.large is an entry-level general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It features a single physical core exposed as 2 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading, accompanied by 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz. This establishes a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of AWS general-purpose platforms. Hardware acceleration capabilities include Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512 instruction sets, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache.

A key architectural component of the m8id.large is its integrated local NVMe SSD storage providing 118 GB of direct disk capacity. The instance lacks discrete GPU acceleration and operates on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the high-clocked Intel core delivers strong single-threaded performance, placing in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core (score of 2162.0), gzip compression (33.96 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (14.43 GB/sec).

Because the instance configuration is restricted to 2 vCPUs sharing a single physical core, aggregate multi-threaded metrics fall in lower benchmark percentiles. Multi-core Geekbench reached 2695.0, while PassMark CPU achieved 4065.66. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is also constrained at 22.4 GB/sec for reads and 15.48 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, network- and throughput-bound services such as static web serving (4.96 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (3.76 million operations/sec) demonstrate weak relative throughput due to the small footprint.

Cost efficiency is driven by the bundling of low-latency local NVMe storage and modern DDR5 memory on a small instance boundary, preventing the need for separate provisioned storage volumes for transient data. Amazon Web Services m8id.large fits microservices, single-threaded batch processing, temporary cache layers, lightweight web servers, and local database development workloads requiring direct NVMe performance without massive multi-core concurrency.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.large is a general-purpose Nitro instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single Intel Xeon 6975P-C physical core running at 3.9 GHz, 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory, and a 118 GB local NVMe SSD. It features modern x86_64 extensions including AVX-512 and AMX, accompanied by a 480 MB L3 cache and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal strong single-core capabilities, registering top-quartile results in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. However, aggregate processing is bound by the dual-vCPU count, showing lower performance in multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth, and large-scale synthetic database tasks. With bundled high-speed local disk storage and balanced compute resources, the m8id.large serves lightweight production workloads, development databases, temporary data caching, and applications requiring rapid local scratch space.
